items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: But a few of them had been out there including Dink Johnson and maybe Bill Johnson had a little trio at first as far as I can understand out in Los Angeles.

ctx.x: Chicago. Chicago. Then later he went to Los Angeles and died out there and made some records with Ori, or maybe not records, he made some radio appearances for Orson Welles, which he only really knew Arlene's band, type band he played with, say six or seven pieces for many years. He made them for this group with Mud Carey and Zutty Singleton as the drummer. So I'll hunt up some of those noon notes which are very sketchy too, very unfortunately. Very little is known about his life. I mentioned about Norwood…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: And his brother Dink was a little bit darker.

ctx.x: Is he kind of brown? No, he's just... Lots of Mexicans, you know, are kind of dark. No, he's just light.

Light, of course, I have one. My skin is like baby skin. You can't say anybody's as white as me, but he's just as light as you are, actually, just about, really. Oh, thank you. He's very light. And his brother Dink was a little bit darker. But you know Don, Don Alba looks white, wouldn't you say? Pretty much so.
Yeah, he looks... His daughter, he has a daughter about nine or ten, and he's a little lighter.
